Subject: Notice: ByteStream Labs — proposed subprocessor + DPA change request

Hi Tessa,

Quick heads up — Stellarus is planning to engage a small analytics vendor, ByteStream Labs, to handle ephemeral logs and metrics for our new pilot. They would be a subprocessor of Redwood for the Stellarus account and will process non-PII operational logs only.

Could you confirm what you need from us to add ByteStream as an approved subprocessor? Specifically:
- DPA amendment / annex how-to and timeline
- Any MSA flow-down language you require (order form impact)
- Evidence we should collect from ByteStream (SOC2, pen test, sub-subcontractors)

I'm attaching their SOW and a brief security summary. We need a decision on permissibility and any order-form billing changes before we kick off integration (target week of Nov 29).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Elena
Elena Bianchi
Head of Platform Integrations
Stellarus Therapeutics

Subject: Re: Notice: ByteStream Labs — proposed subprocessor + DPA change request

Thanks Tessa — reviewed the SOW and the summary. Initial legal take below; I am attaching a draft redline for the MSA and a DPA annex for subprocessor additions.

Summary of required items:
- DPA Annex: add ByteStream to the subprocessor registry via an annex and require a subprocessor-specific Data Processing Addendum (DPA) flow-down for the limited processing (operational logs only).
- MSA / Order Form: insert a flow-down clause for subprocessors referencing the DPA annex; create an Order Form amendment template that lists the subprocessor, scope (logs/metrics), and any billing line if we charge onboarding.
- Evidence gating: require ByteStream SOC2 Type II (within last 12 months) OR a completed short security questionnaire + recent pen test report for the limited scope. Also request their sub-subcontractor list.
- Security controls: require AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, and KV-cache isolation for tenant data (already standard; flagged for ops to confirm).

Approval path:
1) Procurement completes risk rating (low/medium/high) and recommends acceptance or mitigations.
2) Legal approves redline; if high risk, escalate to Legal Director and Security.
3) Contract amendment signed (MSA addendum + DPA annex).

I've uploaded a draft: redline_msa_dpa_draft.docx (link below). The draft includes an Order Form amendment template and a one-paragraph customer-facing acknowledgement to be appended to the order form.

Next steps: Priyom — can you run the vendor risk check and advise if a PO/offboarding/escrow should be required? Marissa/Neha — ops/regulatory: review the controls ask and tell us if any EU residency or local law constraints apply.

Link (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/u/0/folders/1a2B-Subproc-Redlines

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_msa_dpa_draft.docx (docx)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice: ByteStream Labs — procurement risk note

Ran ByteStream through our intake — summary below.

Vendor snapshot:
- ByteStream Labs (analytics): privately held, ~22 employees, primarily US-based.
- Risk rating: Low-to-Medium for operational logs only (no PII).
- Financial: small fixed onboarding fee likely; they requested a standard 30-day payment term in SOW.

Procurement recommendations:
- Accept with standard mitigations: require SOC2 Type II OR completed security questionnaire + recent pen test; require notice of sub-subcontractors; include a 30-day termination for convenience in the Order Form amendment if data-handling scope changes.
- Billing: recommend adding an "analytics integration" one-time fee line in the Order Form and treat recurring usage as part of existing hosting/throughput lines unless ByteStream materially changes token processing patterns.
- Approvals needed: procurement sign-off for vendor, legal sign-off on redline (Kim), AM (Tessa) to confirm customer acceptance.

Uploading procurement note. If legal wants a stricter control we can push for escrow or additional SLAs, but for this scope the standard approach should suffice.

Regards,
Priyom
Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: procurement_note.pdf (pdf)

2) Redwood (Legal/Procurement): we'll share the redline and procurement note. Target for internal sign-off: 10 business days from today (by Nov 28).
3) Contracting: assuming evidence is acceptable, we'll prepare an MSA addendum + DPA annex and an Order Form amendment for signature.

I've attached the draft redline to review; feedback from Stellarus welcome. If you'd like to discuss, I've included a Calendly link here: https://calendly.com/tessa-redwood/30min

Thanks — looking forward to getting ByteStream onboarded cleanly.
